analysis.investment_thesis: NephroPlus operates India's largest dialysis network — a structurally underpenetrated market with a massive addressable patient base as CKD burden rises with urbanisation and diabetes — but at 74.7x trailing P/E with a 13.4% ROE, the stock is priced for perfection before profitability has even matured. Wait for valuation to compress or for ROE to cross 18-20% before building a meaningful position.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 27.5% over 4 years with powerful operating leverage — EBIT grew from 37 Cr (2021) to 167 Cr (2025), a 45.8% CAGR
Dialysis is a chronic, recurring-revenue model — once a patient is on dialysis they need it 3x/week for life, creating predictable, sticky cash flows
Promoter holding at 63.85% with Debt/Equity of only 0.36 and OCF tripling to 135 Cr in FY25 — financial discipline improving
key_risks: Trailing P/E of 74.7x is 3x above my comfort zone — even forward P/E of 28x requires flawless execution to justify; any growth stumble will halve this stock
ROE of 13.4% and ROCE of 14.1% are mediocre — high capex burn (101 Cr in FY25) means returns on capital remain well below my 20%+ threshold for high-conviction bets

FCF only just turned positive in FY25 at a modest 35 Cr — the business is still in heavy investment mode, and any slowdown in center additions or reimbursement rate changes under government PMNDP scheme could derail the story
red_flags: Net losses in FY22 (-21 Cr) and FY23 (-12 Cr) — only 2 years of profitability; the earnings base is too thin to support a 5,260 Cr market cap confidently
Equity jumped from 247 Cr (2021) to 717 Cr (2022) suggesting a large dilutive fundraise — promoters used equity capital to fund growth, minority shareholders bore dilution risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
NephroPlus has built India's most recognisable dialysis brand with genuine scale advantages — bulk procurement, clinical protocols, and a hub-and-spoke model that makes it harder for small operators to compete. The structural case is compelling: India has 200,000+ new ESRD patients annually against grossly insufficient dialysis capacity, and government schemes like PMNDP are expanding reimbursed access. Revenue has compounded at 27.5% and the business has gone from near-breakeven to 67 Cr net profit and 135 Cr OCF in just two years — this is real operational maturation, not accounting fluff.

However, as Jhunjhunwala, I cannot chase this at 74.7x earnings. ROE of 13.4% tells me the business is still consuming capital faster than it generates returns — capex was 101 Cr in FY25 versus 135 Cr OCF, leaving thin FCF of 35 Cr. For a company with a 5,260 Cr market cap, I need to see ROE move convincingly above 18%, FCF yield above 2%, and the forward P/E settle closer to 20x before I take a large position. The international ops (Uzbekistan, Saudi, Philippines) are interesting but add execution complexity for what is still a relatively young listed entity. This is a watchlist stock — the thesis is intact, the price is not.
